context_title: fix all error: Here is the exhaustive, linebyline technical error list for index.html: 2. — Deprecated/nonstandard meta tag; modern browsers and PWA specs use the Web App Manifest for this capability instead. 3. — Deprecated since iOS 15.4 in favor of display field in the Web App Manifest. 4. — Deprecated; replaced by theme-color meta and manifest display settings. 5. — Same generic value as , does not distinguish the app. 6. <link rel="manifest" href="/static/manifest.json"> — No fallback or error handling if the manifest file fails to load; the file path is an absolute URL which will fail in local/filesystem contexts. 7. <link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/static/icon-180.png"> — Duplicate appletouchicon declaration without a sizes attribute followed by a version that does specify sizes="180x180"; the first (unsized) one is redundant. 8. <link rel="icon" sizes="192x192" href="/static/icon-192.png"> — Using rel="icon" with sizes="192x192" is incorrect; sizes on rel="icon" is only valid for ICO or SVG icons per spec; PNG icons should use rel="apple-touch-icon" or be referenced via the manifest. 9. Inline SVG favicon in <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="image/svg+xml,..."> — The SVG uses singlequoted attributes inside a href="..." attribute value, creating a fragile HTML escaping situation that may not parse correctly in all browsers. 10. <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/highlight.js/11.9.0/styles/github-dark-dimmed.min.css"> — Loaded synchronously in <head>, renderblocking. Should use media="print" onload="this.media='all'" or a similar async technique. 11. <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/highlight.js/11.9.0/highlight.min.js"></script> — Loaded synchronously without defer or async, blocking HTML parsing. 12. Both CDN resources (highlight.js CSS + JS) lack crossorigin and integrity attributes — no Subresource Integrity (SRI) check, making the app vulnerable to CDN supplychain compromise. 13. :root defines both --acc: #0071e3 and --accent: #0071e3 — duplicate variables with different names pointing to the same value. --acc is never used later in the code; dead variable. 14. :root defines both --blue: #0071e3 and --accent: #0071e3 — all three (--blue, --acc, --accent) are the same value, creating redundancy and maintenance confusion. 15. --glass: rgba(20,20,24,0.72) — defined in :root but never referenced anywhere in the stylesheet or JavaScript. Dead CSS variable. 16. --user-bg: #0071e3 — also identical to --blue, --acc, and --accent. Four CSS variables with the same value, none consolidated. 17. --liquid-glass, --liquid-border, --liquid-shadow, --glow — defined in both :root (dark) and the light mode @media block, but --liquid-glass, --liquid-border, and --liquid-shadow are never referenced in any CSS rule in the file. Dead variables. 18. @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) overrides do not redefine --glass, --user-bg, --acc, --accent, --blue, --blue-l — these values remain darktheme values in light mode, causing potential contrast/color issues. 19. html, body { overflow: hidden; } — completely disables scrolling on the root elements. If JS fails to initialize the scroll container, the entire page content becomes inaccessible. 20. body { background: #000; } — hardcodes black background directly on body instead of using a CSS variable, inconsistent with the variablebased theming approach used everywhere else. 21. @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) { body { background: #f5f5f7; } } — again uses a hardcoded hex value instead of var(--bg), inconsistent with the rest of the design system. 22. @supports (border-radius: 18px) — This @supports query tests for border-radius support, which has 100% browser support since ~2012. This check is meaningless and dead code; every modern browser satisfies it. 23. The .orb elements use contain: strict — with position: absolute inside a position: fixed parent (#bg), contain: strict creates a new containing block that may interfere with fixed children rendering correctly in some browsers. 24. #app { height: 100vh; min-height: 100dvh; } — uses both 100vh and 100dvh. On mobile browsers 100vh can be larger than the actual visible area (due to address bar), potentially causing overflow. Should use 100dvh alone with 100vh as a fallback, not both. 25. #sidebar { backdrop-filter: blur(60px) saturate(200%) brightness(92%); } — extremely heavy GPU filter on a fullscreen element. No @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) disables this, causing performance issues on lowend devices. 26. #sidebar { transition: transform 420ms cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1.18); } — The cubicbezier value (0.32, 0.72, 0, 1.18) has a control point y=1.18 > 1 which causes the element to overshoot (spring bounce), but only in the closing direction; may feel inconsistent with open animation. 27. #sb-search-bar uses both height: 0 / height: 54px for show/hide and later visibility: hidden / visibility: visible — two separate mechanisms controlling the same element's visibility. The height transition and visibility toggle are redundant and can cause race conditions. 28. #sb-q-cancel { width: 0; opacity: 0; } — sets width: 0 with pointer-events: none for the hidden state. A later rule sets pointer-events: none again redundantly: #sb-q-cancel { pointer-events: none; }. 29. #sb-search-bar.open #sb-q-cancel { pointer-events: auto; } — this rule appears in one section of the CSS but is then contradicted by the earlier unconditional rule #sb-q-cancel { pointer-events: none; }, relying on cascade order for correctness. Fragile; should use specificity or explicit conditions. 30. .hcard-del, .t-row { pointer-events: none; } followed by .hcard:hover .hcard-del, .hcard:focus-within .hcard-del, ... — hoverdependent interactivity. On touch devices, hover states don't fire reliably. The @media (pointer: coarse) rule at the bottom partially addresses this for .hcard-del only, not for .t-row. 31. .t-row { opacity: 0; } — action buttons (copy, retry) are invisible unless the user hovers the message. On mobile/touch, these actions are permanently hidden unless the context menu (longpress) is used. This is a UX dead end for the copy button, as users cannot access it without hover or longpress. 32. #sidebar[aria-hidden="true"] { pointer-events: none; } and #sidebar[aria-hidden="false"] { pointer-events: auto; } — these attribute selectors only take effect after the IIFE sets the attribute. During page load before JS runs, the sidebar has no aria-hidden attribute and falls into neither rule, so pointer-events is unset (default auto), meaning the sidebar intercepts clicks before JS initialises. 33. #stb { bottom: 96px; } — hardcodes 96px for the scrolltobottom button's position. This is then dynamically overridden by JS (stb.style.bottom = ...), making the CSS value a dead default that will only briefly appear before JS sets it correctly. 34. .md h1 { font-size: 17.5px; } — uses px instead of rem or em, breaking user fontsize preferences and accessibility zoom scaling. 35. .md h2 { font-size: 15.5px; } — same issue: hardcoded px value. 36. .md h3 { font-size: 14px; } — same issue. 37. .hcard-pre mark { background: rgba(0,113,227,.22); color: var(--blue-l); } — in light mode, --blue-l is not redefined in the lightmode media query override, so it keeps the darkmode value #147CE5. This may have insufficient contrast on the light surface. 38. .cb pre code { font-family: 'SF Mono', Menlo, Monaco, 'Courier New', monospace; } — SF Mono is an Appleonly font. On nonApple platforms, falls back to Menlo (also Appleonly), then Monaco (also Appleonly), before reaching 'Courier New'. Windows/Linux users get Courier New or a generic monospace — no crossplatform neutral choice like Consolas or Cascadia Code is included. 39. .cb-hdr { background: #181820; } — hardcoded hex value ignoring the CSS variable system; will not adapt to light mode, rendering a dark header in light mode. 40. .cb pre code { background: #14141a; } — same problem: hardcoded dark hex for code background, will not adapt to light mode. 41. @keyframes drift uses will-change: transform on .orb — will-change is a hint, not a guarantee, and applying it to multiple elements simultaneously can consume excess GPU memory on mobile. 42. @keyframes bubbleIn and @keyframes aiBubbleIn are defined but both use very similar transforms; bubbleIn is applied to both .u .bubble (via animation property) and .typing (via animation: bubbleIn .32s...). If a future CSS change aliases these, both animations change unintentionally. Should be named more specifically. 43. The @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) rule at the bottom uses animation: none !important — this is correct, but it overrides all animations including @keyframes td (typing dots), @keyframes drift (background orbs), and @keyframes bubbleIn. However, the typing dots (td animation) being disabled with !important means the .rc-dot.done state's animation: none rule is also !importantoverridden at all times on reducedmotion, which is a noop collision rather than a bug, but adds confusion. 44. :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--blue-l); } — --blue-l is #147CE5 in dark mode. This is not redefined in the lightmode media query, so in light mode the focus ring is still #147CE5 on a light background. Contrast ratio may be insufficient for WCAG AA on light surfaces. 45. const SK = 'cs_v4', HK = 'ch_v4', DK = 'cgd_v1'; — localStorage keys are defined as modulelevel constants. If the version suffixes need to change (e.g., data structure migration), there is no migration logic; old keys are simply abandoned in localStorage, causing stale data accumulation. 46. const $ = id => document.getElementById(id); — shadows the global jQuery shorthand $ if jQuery were ever added, but more importantly, it does not throw or warn if the element is not found; callers may get null and immediately call a method on it, crashing silently. 47. const sa = $('scroll-area'), ml = $('msg-list'), ta = $('ta'), sbtn = $('sbtn'), sico = $('sico'), stb = $('stb'), istrip = $('img-strip'); — all these are set at script execution time (toplevel IIFE), before the DOM is guaranteed to be parsed at that position. Since the <script> is at the bottom of <body> this works, but there is no DOMContentLoaded guard, making it fragile if script position ever changes. 48. new ResizeObserver(() => { setIBH(); if (nearBot()) goBot(); }).observe($('ib-wrap')); — the ResizeObserver callback is created with no error handling. If $('ib-wrap') is null, .observe(null) throws a TypeError. 49. window.visualViewport.addEventListener('resize', syncVV) — window.visualViewport can be null in nonbrowser environments and certain embedded WebViews. Although guarded by if (window.visualViewport), it immediately accesses .addEventListener without rechecking inside, which is fine, but document.addEventListener('focusout', () => { setTimeout(syncVV, 80); }, { passive: true }) is registered unconditionally, even if visualViewport is absent, causing syncVV to call setIBH() when it may not be needed. 50. window.__saScrollTimer — uses a global property on window for debounce timer ID. This pollutes the global namespace and can conflict with other scripts. 51. function openSB() calls renderHist() — renderHist() accesses $('hlist') which could be null if called before DOM is ready. No null guard inside renderHist() beyond a single early return. 52. let searchRenderTimer = 0; — uses 0 as a sentinel for "no timer active". clearTimeout(0) is technically valid (noop), but semantically misleading; null is cleaner and conventional. 53. $('sb-q').addEventListener('input', ...) and $('sb-q-cancel').addEventListener('click', ...) — these are called at module toplevel, assuming the elements exist. No nullguard. 54. document.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if ((e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) && e.key.toLowerCase() === 'f') { e.preventDefault(); ... } }) — overrides the browser's native find (Ctrl+F / Cmd+F). While intentional, this is an aggressive UX override that breaks standard browser accessibility for users who rely on native text search. 55. Inside initPullToSearch, const body = document.querySelector('.sb-body') — if .sb-body doesn't exist, body is null, and body.addEventListener(...) throws a TypeError. 56. initPullToSearch references openSearch before openSearch is defined in the code (defined later as a function declaration) — works due to function hoisting, but the implicit dependency on ordering is a maintenance hazard. 57. const sidebar = $('sidebar'); — declared at module level again (also declared inside initPullToSearch as const sidebar = $('sidebar')). This is a redeclaration of the same name in two different scopes, which is confusing but not a runtime bug since they're in separate scopes; however it creates a shadowing situation inside the IIFE. 58. document.addEventListener('touchmove', e => { ... }, { passive: true }) for sidebar dragging — passive: true prevents calling e.preventDefault() inside. Since no preventDefault is called, this is fine; but if any future modification needs to prevent scroll during drag, this will silently fail. 59. document.addEventListener('touchend', e => { ... }, { passive: true }) — same note as above; also e.changedTouches[0] is accessed without checking that e.changedTouches.length > 0, which could throw on synthetic or cancelled touch events. 60. const SB_EDGE_ZONE = 36; — magic number with no comment explaining its origin (pixels from left edge for swipetoopen gesture zone). 61. In the touchend handler: if (dx > tapThreshold && tsX < SB_EDGE_ZONE && !sbOpen) openSB(); — this check fires on every touchend, not just when sbDragging was false. If the user did a short tap anywhere on the left edge without triggering the drag path, the sidebar might open unexpectedly. There's no minimum drag velocity check. 62. function toast(msg, type = 'inf', ms = 3000) — the icons object has keys err, ok, inf. If type is any other value (e.g., 'warn', 'success'), icons[type] is undefined and the fallback icons.inf is used silently. No validation or warning. 63. In toast(): t.appendChild(iconWrap.firstChild) — iconWrap.firstChild could be null if innerHTML results in an empty/textonly node. appendChild(null) throws a TypeError. 64. function escHtml(s) — does not escape backticks ( ` ). While backticks are not HTMLspecial characters, they can be problematic in attribute values (e.g., in template literals or certain parsing contexts). Minor/theoretical but worth noting. 65. function applyInlineMd(s) — does not escape HTML before applying inline markdown. If s contains raw < or > characters (e.g., from user input), they are inserted as raw HTML into the code placeholder tokens and then restored unescaped, creating a potential markup injection vector in the search highlight context where this function is called. 66. applyInlineMd inline code replacement uses \x1e as a sentinel character — if the input string actually contains \x1e (a valid Unicode control character), it will be misinterpreted as a code placeholder, corrupting output. 67. function parseTableRow(row) — the inCode toggle logic uses a simple boolean flag and toggles on every backtick. Nested backticks (e.g., `` code `` ) are not handled; the flag will be toggled twice, resulting in incorrectly treating content outside backtick pairs as code. 68. function renderTable(raw) — if (rows.length < 3) return escHtml(raw) — returns the raw escaped source if there are fewer than 3 rows. This means a table with just a header row and separator (2 rows, which is the minimum valid Markdown table) is never rendered as a table; minimum is enforced as 3. 69. In renderTable: rows.slice(2) — assumes index 0 is header, index 1 is separator, index 2+ are body rows. No validation that row 1 actually is a separator row; any nonseparator line is silently skipped but its position is still consumed. 70. function sanitizeHref(rawHref) — the regex ^(?:https?:|mailto:|tel:|\\/(?!\\/)|#) tests the beginning of the string. It does not prevent javascript: URIs that are obfuscated with whitespace (e.g., \tjavascript:alert(1)) before trimming. Although .trim() is applied before the test, Unicode whitespace (e.g., \u00A0, \u2003) is not removed by .trim() in some older environments. 71. function replaceMdLinks(s) — the label extracted from [label] is inserted into <a ...>${label}</a> without HTMLescaping. If label contains <img> or <script> fragments, they are rendered as raw HTML. 72. In md(): s = s.replace(/((?:^[^\n|]*\|[^\n]+\|?[ \t]*(?:\n|$)){3,})/gm, match => { ... }) — this regex for detecting tables runs before escHtml(), meaning the table raw content is not escaped when matched. If the table cell content contains <, >, or &, these flow through to renderTable() where escHtml() is applied — but the regex also matches nontable |containing lines (e.g., code comments with pipe characters), potentially misidentifying code as tables. 73. In md(): s = s.replace(/```([^\n`]*)\n?([\s\S]*?)(?:```(?=\n|$)|$)/g, ...) — the regex uses $ as an alternative closing delimiter for fenced code blocks. This means an unclosed code fence at the end of the input silently consumes the rest of the document into the code block, swallowing all subsequent markdown content. 74. In md(): after escaping with escHtml(s), inline code is reextracted. But the backtick pattern is /`([^`\n]+)`/g — this does not handle code spans that span multiple lines (e.g., in some markdown flavors) and does not handle escaped backticks (\). 75. In md(): s = s.replace(/__([\\s\\S]+?)__/g, '<strong>$1</strong>') — applied after escHtml(), meaning the matched content $1 is already HTMLescaped, but the injected <strong> tags are raw HTML. This is correct behavior, but if $1 itself contains leftover sentinel characters or partial tags, it could corrupt markup. 76. In md(): The heading regex s = s.replace(/^#\s*(.+)$/gm, '<h1>$1</h1>') — captures $1 which may contain alreadypartiallyprocessed inline markdown (bold, italic, code placeholders). Since $1 is not further processed for nested inlines after heading replacement, inline formatting inside headings is not rendered. For example # **Bold Heading** renders the literal **Bold Heading** inside <h1>. 77. The md() function processes inline code, bold, italic, and headings by replacing patterns in the string sequentially. But there is a logical ordering issue: escHtml() is called before inline code extraction, meaning backtickenclosed content has its HTML already escaped and is then replaced as a raw <span>. However, if the escaped content includes <, the code span displays literal < correctly — but the escaping of & to & inside code spans results in doubleescaping: & displayed to user as & instead of &. 78. In md() list processing: const um = l.match(/^\s*[-*+]\s*(.+)$/), om = l.match(/^\s*\d+\.\s*(.+)$/) — the matched content um[1] and om[1] are inserted directly as <li>${um[1]}</li> without applying inline markdown processing (bold, italic, links, code spans). List item content is rendered as plain text. 79. In md(): const blockRe = /<\/?(?:h[1-3]|ul|ol|li|hr|table|thead|tbody|tr|th|td)\b/i; — used to determine whether a paragraph segment contains block HTML. Splits on \n\n+ but uses .filter(x => x.trim()) — this means a segment that is purely whitespace is dropped, which could cause a missing paragraph break between two blocks. 80. In md(): for (let i = 0; i < tables.length; i++) { const ph = '|TABLE_${i}|'; ... s = s.replace('<p>${ph}</p>', tableHtml); s = s.replace(ph, tableHtml); } — the placeholder |TABLE_0| contains | characters. If the table placeholder happens to match an actual |TABLE_0| string in the original document (extremely unlikely but possible), it causes incorrect replacement. 81. window.cpcode = btn => { ... } — exposes a function on the global window object from within an IIFE. This leaks into the global namespace, which is an antipattern especially since the entire script is wrapped in an IIFE to avoid exactly this. 82. window.buildDownloadName = buildDownloadName; — same issue: deliberately exposes an internal utility to global scope from within the IIFE, inconsistent with the IIFE encapsulation pattern. 83. function ftime() — returns a localeformatted time string using toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' }). Passing an empty array [] as the locale falls back to the system locale, which is fine, but no timeZone is specified, so the time reflects the user's local time zone — which is correct for a chat UI but undocumented. 84. function normalizeWhitespace(s) { return String(s || '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim(); } — collapses all whitespace including newlines, which destroys multiline structure when used for getGroupCoreText(). This affects the deletegroup keying mechanism: two messages with the same text but different whitespace structure get the same key and may be incorrectly identified as duplicates. 85. function safeSliceText(value, maxChars) { return Array.from(String(value || '')).slice(0, maxChars).join(''); } — uses Array.from() for Unicodesafe slicing, which is correct. However maxChars has no default value; if called without a second argument, slice(0, undefined) returns the full array — no truncation occurs. The function name implies safety but silently does nothing if maxChars is omitted. 86. In highlightPreviewText: const start = norm.indexOf(queryNorm); if (start === -1) return escHtml(raw); — only highlights the first match. If the query appears multiple times in the text, only the first occurrence is marked. 87. In buildUserDisplayText: file names are prepended with 📎 emoji. If a file name contains HTMLspecial characters (<, >, &, "), they are not escaped before being used as textContent in the display bubble — however mkUserGroup uses .textContent = text, so this is safe for the bubble. But in the hmeta.preview which ends up in renderHist() with escHtml, the emoji and file names go through escHtml — 📎 survives but < in a filename would be escaped, which is correct. 88. function cloneTextAttachments(atts) — performs a shallow clone of each attachment object. If att.content were ever an object rather than a string (e.g., due to a bug upstream), the clone would share the reference. This is a defensive programming gap. 89. function dataUrlToImgPayload(dataUrl) — the regex ^([^;]+);base64,(.+)$ matches the entire string with .+ for the base64 data part. For very large images (multiMB base64 strings), this regex must process the entire string, which can be slow. 90. function urlToDataUrl(url) — if (!url || /^/i.test(url)) return url; — if url is already a data URL, it returns a string, not a Promise resolving to a string (the function is async, so returning a nonPromise value resolves the returned Promise; this is fine). But if url is falsy, it returns undefined (falsy), which is inconsistently typed compared to the nonfalsy path which returns a string URL. 91. In urlToDataUrl: const contentType = (resp.headers.get('content-type') || '').toLowerCase(); then if (!contentType.startsWith('image/')) throw new Error('Fetched resource is not an image'); — this check is a good validation, but the contentType may include parameters like image/jpeg; charset=... which still starts with image/, so the check passes. A URL returning image/jpeg; boundary=... (malformed) would also pass. Minor edge case. 92. async function ensureImgPayloads(payload) — if both payload.imgPay and payload.imageUrls are present and nonempty, only imgPay is used and imageUrls is ignored. No warning or comment explains this priority choice. 93. function clearComposerAttachments() — resets imgs = [] and textAtts = [] but these are closure variables in the outer IIFE. If any ongoing operation holds a reference to the old arrays (e.g., an inprogress send() call captured const ic = [...imgs]), those references remain valid. However, if clearComposerAttachments() is called midsend, the imgs reference in send() was already spread before the clear, so this is actually safe — but the pattern is fragile. 94. async function populateComposerFromPayload(payload) — calls clearComposerAttachments() at the start, which resets imgs and textAtts. If called while a message is streaming, it clears the attachment state silently without notifying the user. 95. In compress(): const ctx = c.getContext('2d'); if (!ctx) { rej(new Error('Canvas context unavailable')); return; } — getContext('2d') can return null if the browser is in a headless/privacy mode that blocks canvas. The error is rejected correctly, but callers of compress() do not all have .catch() handlers — in handleFiles() the try/catch wraps the entire sequence, so this is caught. But addThumb() is also called separately; it does not use canvas but could still be affected by surrounding logic. 96. function addThumb(url) — the img-rm button uses textContent: '✕'. The ✕ character (U+2715) may not render correctly on all systems; using an SVG icon (as done elsewhere in the code) would be more consistent. 97. The img-rm button inside addFileChip also uses textContent: '✕' (via innerHTML) — same inconsistency. 98. In addFileChip: chip.innerHTML = '...<span class="file-chip-name">${att.name}</span>...' — att.name is a filename from a userselected file. It is inserted into innerHTML without escaping. If the filename contains <, >, &, or ", it creates malformed HTML or an injection vector. 99. In handleFiles(): const ext = nameLow.includes('.') ? nameLow.split('.').pop() : nameLow; — split('.').pop() on a file named .eslintrc returns eslintrc (correct), but on file.tar.gz returns gz (correct), and on file. returns '' (empty string). An empty extension is then looked up in TEXT_EXTS (not found), so isText would be false unless the MIME type triggers it — edge case but potential misidentification. 100. $('btn-gal').addEventListener('click', () => $('fg').click()) — $('fg') could return null if the element doesn't exist, causing null.click() to throw. 101. ta.addEventListener('paste', async (e) => { ... }) — calls e.preventDefault() conditionally (only if there are image items). But the check for pastedText and insertion via insertTextAtCursor happens after e.preventDefault(), which prevents the browser's default text paste. Then insertTextAtCursor(pastedText) is called manually. However, if the clipboard has both text and an image, this works — but if pastedText is empty but imgItems is nonempty, insertTextAtCursor('') is called with an empty string, which is a noop but wasteful. If the clipboard has text but no images, the function returns early without calling e.preventDefault(), which is correct. But there is a subtle bug: imgItems.length is checked before the early return; the early return if (!imgItems.length) return; happens before e.preventDefault() — so textonly paste is unaffected. This is correct. But the pastedText read from clipboard and e.preventDefault() — if pastedText has value and imgItems is nonempty, the browser default text insertion is prevented and manual insertion is done. This is intentional but means the user cannot use browser paste undo (Ctrl+Z) after this event. 102. In grow(): const needsShrink = ta.scrollHeight < current - 4; — computes current = ta.offsetHeight before any height changes. If ta.style.height = 'auto' causes a relayout, offsetHeight would need to be reread. Since it's read before the conditional if (needsShrink), the stale current could cause incorrect shrink detection. 103. ta.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey) { e.preventDefault(); if (!sbtn.disabled) send(); } }) — on mobile soft keyboards, Enter key events may not fire consistently; the keydown listener may not receive Enter on all mobile browsers/keyboards (some send composition events instead). The send button is the primary mobile action. 104. function stop() — calls ctrl.abort() then sets ctrl = null. If ctrl is already null (e.g., called twice), ctrl.abort() throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of null. No null guard. 105. async function send() — the check if ((!text && !imgs.length && !textAtts.length) || streaming) return; guards against empty sends. But imgs and textAtts are checked at the start of send(), then immediately spread into ic and currentTextAtts. If another async operation modifies imgs between the check and the spread, the guard could fail. This is a theoretical race condition. 106. In send(): const ic = [...imgs]; imgs = []; — reassigns the modulelevel imgs array. Any part of the code that cached a reference to the old array retains stale data. Should use imgs.splice(0) to clear in place, or consistently use the spreadandreassign pattern throughout. 107. ta.value = ''; ta.style.height = 'auto'; inside send() — clears the textarea before the async network operation. If the network request fails immediately (synchronously or in the first microtask), the user's input is lost with no recovery. 108. In send(): msgs.push({ role: 'user', content: fullText, ts: Date.now(), imgPay: payload.map(item => ({ ...item })), rawText: text, imageUrls: [...ic], textAtts: currentTextAtts, agentMode }) — note agentMode is the bare variable (shorthand property). This captures the current agentMode value. If agentMode changes while streaming (e.g., user toggles agent mode), the persisted message has the old value. This is technically correct, but the lack of explicit agentMode: agentMode notation makes it less readable. 109. function processSSEEvent(block, ctx) — const dataLines = String(block || '').split('\n').filter(line => line.startsWith('')); — if a field spans multiple lines (per SSE spec, continuation lines start with a space), multiline SSE data is not handled. Only singleline data values are parsed. 110. In processSSEEvent: let ev; try { ev = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (_) { return; } — silently discards malformed JSON events with no logging. Makes debugging serverside issues very difficult. 111. In processSSEEvent, ev.type === 'search_done': else Object.entries(ctx.srchBars).forEach(([k, el]) => { if (k.startsWith('id:')) markSrchDone(el); }); — if ev.query is an empty string (falsy but valid), the else branch runs and marks ALL idkeyed search bars done, potentially incorrectly marking unrelated searches as done. 112. In streamReq: const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => { try { abortController.abort(); } catch (_) {} }, 90000); — 90second timeout is hardcoded with no way to configure it. For very slow servers or large responses, this may prematurely abort a valid longrunning stream. 113. In streamReq: let resp = await fetch(apiUrl, { ... }) — the AbortController signal is passed, but if abortController.abort() is called before fetch resolves, the AbortError is caught in the catch block. However, the clearTimeout(timeoutId) is in finally, which is correct. But the timeout callback also calls abortController.abort() which may fire after the finally block completes if there is a race — clearTimeout in finally prevents this correctly. 114. In streamReq: if (resp.status === 204 || !resp.body) — resp.body is a ReadableStream object, which is always truthy even for empty streams. Checking !resp.body would never be true in browsers that implement the Fetch API. This condition effectively only handles status 204. 115. In streamReq: buf += dec.decode(value, { stream: true }); inside the reader loop, then buf += dec.decode(); after the loop — this is the correct pattern for TextDecoder streaming. However, buf can grow unbounded if the server sends an enormous response before any \n\n separator is found, potentially consuming large amounts of memory. 116. In streamReq catch block: const delay = Math.min(12000, 1400 * (2 ** (retries - 1))) + Math.round(Math.random() * 350); — exponential backoff calculation. When retries = 1: 1400 * 2^0 = 1400ms. When retries = 2: 1400 * 2^1 = 2800ms. When retries = 3: 1400 * 2^2 = 5600ms. These are all under 12000ms, so the Math.min clamp never applies for 3 retries. Dead clamp logic at current retries < 3 limit. 117. In streamReq catch: const noRetry = !!(e && (e._httpStatus === 401 || e._httpStatus === 403)); — only these two status codes disable retry. A 404 (session not found), 429 (rate limited), or 500 (server error) all get retried up to 3 times, which may be wrong for 404 and 429 specifically. 118. In retryFromPayload: if (streaming) return; — silently returns without notifying the user that the retry was skipped because streaming is active. The retry button remains visible and appears nonfunctional. 119. function retryLast() — defined but never called anywhere in the codebase (no event listener, no reference). Dead function. 120. function setAgentMode(value) — ta.placeholder is set to either 'Agent utasítás...' or 'Üzenet'. The Hungarian ellipsis ... is used instead of … (U+2026 HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS). While functional, it is typographically incorrect. 121. function persist() — if (!sid) return; guards against null sid. But localStorage.setItem is called inside a try/catch that swallows all errors silently (including QuotaExceededError when storage is full), giving no user feedback. 122. function newChat() — calls stop(), which calls ctrl.abort(). If ctrl is null at the time of newChat() (no active stream), stop() crashes (see issue 104). 123. In newChat(): if (oldSid && deletedGroups[oldSid]) { delete deletedGroups[oldSid]; persistDeletedGroups(); } — cleans up deletedGroups for the old session. But persistDeletedGroups() calls localStorage.setItem which can throw — wrapped in persistDeletedGroups's try/catch, so this is safe. But the cleanup only happens for the specific oldSid, not for any orphaned sessions whose deletedGroups entry might persist. 124. function updHist() — if (!sid || !msgs.length) return; — if a session has been created and messages sent but then all messages are deleted via the UI, msgs.length is 0 and the history is not updated. The conversation disappears from hmeta on the next updHist() call after deletion. 125. In renderHist(): const highlighted = q ? safe.replace(new RegExp(`(${q.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g,'\\$&')})`, 'gi'), '<mark>$1</mark>') : safe; — inserts <mark>$1</mark> where $1 is captured from the usersupplied (but escaped) query match in the alreadyHTMLescaped safe string. The <mark> tags are inserted as raw HTML markup into innerHTML, which is intentional. However, safe has already been HTMLescaped, and the regex matches based on the escaped string — if the search query contains &, <, >, these are escaped in safe to &, <, >, but the regex escapes q for regex special chars, not HTML chars. So a search for < would need to match < in safe to highlight correctly, but the regex looks for the literal < (after escaping for regex), which won't match <. Result: HTML entities in titles are not highlightable by typing the original character. 126. The highlightPreviewText function (used elsewhere) does handle normalization correctly, but renderHist uses a separate, simpler inline regex approach — inconsistency between two highlighting implementations in the same codebase. 127. async function restoreSid(id) — const r = await fetch('/api/session/${id}'); — id is interpolated directly into the URL string. Although id is a session ID from hmeta which was originally received from the server, there is no encodeURIComponent(id) call, leaving the path injection risk if the id contains special URL characters like / or ?. 128. In restoreSid: the for...of loop iterates data.messages. For very long conversation histories, this runs synchronously without yielding to the browser, potentially causing a long task (janky UI) while restoring a large session. 129. In restoreSid: if (m.role === 'tool' && m.is_tool_result) { ... if (content && content.includes('Search results for:')) { ... const urlMatches = [...content.matchAll(/URL: (https?:\/\/\S+)/g)]; — URL extraction uses \S+ which matches any nonwhitespace including punctuation at the end (e.g., http://example.com. with trailing period). The trailing period would be included in the URL incorrectly. 130. In restoreSid: if (m.has_image && !imgSrcs.length) { const badge = document.createElement('div'); badge.className = 'img-badge'; ... } — the class img-badge is used here but is not defined anywhere in the <style> block. The badge will render without any styling. 131. async function init() — calls localStorage.getItem(HK) and localStorage.getItem(DK) at startup. In private/incognito browsing on some iOS Safari versions, localStorage access throws a SecurityError. Although wrapped in try/catch, the catch block is catch (_) {} — silently ignores the error, leaving hmeta as an empty array (which is the fallback default and acceptable, but undocumented). 132. In init(): const knownSids = new Set(hmeta.map(h => h.sid)); followed by cleanup of deletedGroups entries for unknown sessions — this cleanup only runs on init(). If a session is deleted from the server (via the delete API) but the client still has a deletedGroups entry for it, it is not cleaned until init() runs again (page reload or first load). Minor stale data issue. 133. In init(): hmeta.sort((a, b) => (b.ts || 0) - (a.ts || 0)); — sessions fetched from the server are merged with local hmeta. The ts (timestamp) field from the server's response is used as s.updated_at. If the server returns updated_at as a date string (ISO 8601) rather than a Unix timestamp integer, (b.ts || 0) - (a.ts || 0) performs string subtraction (NaN), breaking the sort. No type validation is performed on s.updated_at. 134. In init(): closeSB() is called at the end, which is correct since the sidebar should start closed. But closeSB() calls closeSearch() which calls $('sb-q').value = '' and $('sb-q').blur() — calling .blur() on an element during page initialization when focus may not be on that element is harmless but unnecessary. 135. The second <script> block (context menu) is outside the IIFE of the first script block. It references functions getGroupCopyText, getUserComposerPayload, populateComposerFromPayload, cptext, send, grow, markDeletedGroup, syncMsgsFromDom, upd

If called while a message is streaming, it clears the attachment state silently without notifying the user. 95. In compress(): const ctx = c.getContext('2d'); if (!ctx) { rej(new Error('Canvas context unavailable')); return; } — getContext('2d') can return null if the browser is in a headless/privacy mode that blocks canvas. The error is rejected correctly, but callers of compress() do not all have .catch() handlers — in handleFiles() the try/catch wraps the entire sequence, so this is caught. But addThumb() is also called separately; it does not use canvas but could still be affected by surrounding logic. 96. function addThumb(url) — the img-rm button uses textContent: '✕'. The ✕ character (U+2715) may not render correctly on all systems; using an SVG icon (as done elsewhere in the code) would be more consistent. 97. The img-rm button inside addFileChip also uses textContent: '✕' (via innerHTML) — same inconsistency. 98. In addFileChip: chip.innerHTML = '...<span class="file-chip-name">${att.name}</span>...' — att.name is a filename from a userselected file. It is inserted into innerHTML without escaping. If the filename contains <, >, &, or ", it creates malformed HTML or an injection vector. 99. In handleFiles(): const ext = nameLow.includes('.') ? nameLow.split('.').pop() : nameLow; — split('.').pop() on a file named .eslintrc returns eslintrc (correct), but on file.tar.gz returns gz (correct), and on file. returns '' (empty string). An empty extension is then looked up in TEXT_EXTS (not found), so isText would be false unless the MIME type triggers it — edge case but potential misidentification. 100. $('btn-gal').addEventListener('click', () => $('fg').click()) — $('fg') could return null if the element doesn't exist, causing null.click() to throw. 101. ta.addEventListener('paste', async (e) => { ... }) — calls e.preventDefault() conditionally (only if there are image items). But the check for pastedText and insertion via insertTextAtCursor happens after e.preventDefault(), which prevents the browser's default text paste. Then insertTextAtCursor(pastedText) is called manually. However, if the clipboard has both text and an image, this works — but if pastedText is empty but imgItems is nonempty, insertTextAtCursor('') is called with an empty string, which is a noop but wasteful. If the clipboard has text but no images, the function returns early without calling e.preventDefault(), which is correct. But there is a subtle bug: imgItems.length is checked before the early return; the early return if (!imgItems.length) return; happens before e.preventDefault() — so textonly paste is unaffected. This is correct. But the pastedText read from clipboard and e.preventDefault() — if pastedText has value and imgItems is nonempty, the browser default text insertion is prevented and manual insertion is done. This is intentional but means the user cannot use browser paste undo (Ctrl+Z) after this event. 102. In grow(): const needsShrink = ta.scrollHeight < current - 4; — computes current = ta.offsetHeight before any height changes. If ta.style.height = 'auto' causes a relayout, offsetHeight would need to be reread. Since it's read before the conditional if (needsShrink), the stale current could cause incorrect shrink detection. 103. ta.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey) { e.preventDefault(); if (!sbtn.disabled) send(); } }) — on mobile soft keyboards, Enter key events may not fire consistently; the keydown listener may not receive Enter on all mobile browsers/keyboards (some send composition events instead). The send button is the primary mobile action. 104. function stop() — calls ctrl.abort() then sets ctrl = null. If ctrl is already null (e.g., called twice), ctrl.abort() throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of null. No null guard. 105. async function send() — the check if ((!text && !imgs.length && !textAtts.length) || streaming) return; guards against empty sends. But imgs and textAtts are checked at the start of send(), then immediately spread into ic and currentTextAtts. If another async operation modifies imgs between the check and the spread, the guard could fail. This is a theoretical race condition. 106. In send(): const ic = [...imgs]; imgs = []; — reassigns the modulelevel imgs array. Any part of the code that cached a reference to the old array retains stale data. Should use imgs.splice(0) to clear in place, or consistently use the spreadandreassign pattern throughout. 107. ta.value = ''; ta.style.height = 'auto'; inside send() — clears the textarea before the async network operation. If the network request fails immediately (synchronously or in the first microtask), the user's input is lost with no recovery. 108. In send(): msgs.push({ role: 'user', content: fullText, ts: Date.now(), imgPay: payload.map(item => ({ ...item })), rawText: text, imageUrls: [...ic], textAtts: currentTextAtts, agentMode }) — note agentMode is the bare variable (shorthand property). This captures the current agentMode value. If agentMode changes while streaming (e.g., user toggles agent mode), the persisted message has the old value. This is technically correct, but the lack of explicit agentMode: agentMode notation makes it less readable. 109. function processSSEEvent(block, ctx) — const dataLines = String(block || '').split('\n').filter(line => line.startsWith('')); — if a field spans multiple lines (per SSE spec, continuation lines start with a space), multiline SSE data is not handled. Only singleline data values are parsed. 110. In processSSEEvent: let ev; try { ev = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (_) { return; } — silently discards malformed JSON events with no logging. Makes debugging serverside issues very difficult. 111. In processSSEEvent, ev.type === 'search_done': else Object.entries(ctx.srchBars).forEach(([k, el]) => { if (k.startsWith('id:')) markSrchDone(el); }); — if ev.query is an empty string (falsy but valid), the else branch runs and marks ALL idkeyed search bars done, potentially incorrectly marking unrelated searches as done. 112. In streamReq: const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => { try { abortController.abort(); } catch (_) {} }, 90000); — 90second timeout is hardcoded with no way to configure it. For very slow servers or large responses, this may prematurely abort a valid longrunning stream. 113. In streamReq: let resp = await fetch(apiUrl, { ... }) — the AbortController signal is passed, but if abortController.abort() is called before fetch resolves, the AbortError is caught in the catch block. However, the clearTimeout(timeoutId) is in finally, which is correct. But the timeout callback also calls abortController.abort() which may fire after the finally block completes if there is a race — clearTimeout in finally prevents this correctly. 114. In streamReq: if (resp.status === 204 || !resp.body) — resp.body is a ReadableStream object, which is always truthy even for empty streams. Checking !resp.body would never be true in browsers that implement the Fetch API. This condition effectively only handles status 204. 115. In streamReq: buf += dec.decode(value, { stream: true }); inside the reader loop, then buf += dec.decode(); after the loop — this is the correct pattern for TextDecoder streaming. However, buf can grow unbounded if the server sends an enormous response before any \n\n separator is found, potentially consuming large amounts of memory. 116. In streamReq catch block: const delay = Math.min(12000, 1400 * (2 ** (retries - 1))) + Math.round(Math.random() * 350); — exponential backoff calculation. When retries = 1: 1400 * 2^0 = 1400ms. When retries = 2: 1400 * 2^1 = 2800ms. When retries = 3: 1400 * 2^2 = 5600ms. These are all under 12000ms, so the Math.min clamp never applies for 3 retries. Dead clamp logic at current retries < 3 limit. 117. In streamReq catch: const noRetry = !!(e && (e._httpStatus === 401 || e._httpStatus === 403)); — only these two status codes disable retry. A 404 (session not found), 429 (rate limited), or 500 (server error) all get retried up to 3 times, which may be wrong for 404 and 429 specifically. 118. In retryFromPayload: if (streaming) return; — silently returns without notifying the user that the retry was skipped because streaming is active. The retry button remains visible and appears nonfunctional. 119. function retryLast() — defined but never called anywhere in the codebase (no event listener, no reference). Dead function. 120. function setAgentMode(value) — ta.placeholder is set to either 'Agent utasítás...' or 'Üzenet'. The Hungarian ellipsis ... is used instead of … (U+2026 HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS). While functional, it is typographically incorrect. 121. function persist() — if (!sid) return; guards against null sid. But localStorage.setItem is called inside a try/catch that swallows all errors silently (including QuotaExceededError when storage is full), giving no user feedback. 122. function newChat() — calls stop(), which calls ctrl.abort(). If ctrl is null at the time of newChat() (no active stream), stop() crashes (see issue 104). 123. In newChat(): if (oldSid && deletedGroups[oldSid]) { delete deletedGroups[oldSid]; persistDeletedGroups(); } — cleans up deletedGroups for the old session. But persistDeletedGroups() calls localStorage.setItem which can throw — wrapped in persistDeletedGroups's try/catch, so this is safe. But the cleanup only happens for the specific oldSid, not for any orphaned sessions whose deletedGroups entry might persist. 124. function updHist() — if (!sid || !msgs.length) return; — if a session has been created and messages sent but then all messages are deleted via the UI, msgs.length is 0 and the history is not updated. The conversation disappears from hmeta on the next updHist() call after deletion. 125. In renderHist(): const highlighted = q ? safe.replace(new RegExp(`(${q.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g,'\\$&')})`, 'gi'), '<mark>$1</mark>') : safe; — inserts <mark>$1</mark> where $1 is captured from the usersupplied (but escaped) query match in the alreadyHTMLescaped safe string. The <mark> tags are inserted as raw HTML markup into innerHTML, which is intentional. However, safe has already been HTMLescaped, and the regex matches based on the escaped string — if the search query contains &, <, >, these are escaped in safe to &, <, >, but the regex escapes q for regex special chars, not HTML chars. So a search for < would need to match < in safe to highlight correctly, but the regex looks for the literal < (after escaping for regex), which won't match <. Result: HTML entities in titles are not highlightable by typing the original character. 126. The highlightPreviewText function (used elsewhere) does handle normalization correctly, but renderHist uses a separate, simpler inline regex approach — inconsistency between two highlighting implementations in the same codebase. 127. async function restoreSid(id) — const r = await fetch('/api/session/${id}'); — id is interpolated directly into the URL string. Although id is a session ID from hmeta which was originally received from the server, there is no encodeURIComponent(id) call, leaving the path injection risk if the id contains special URL characters like / or ?. 128. In restoreSid: the for...of loop iterates data.messages. For very long conversation histories, this runs synchronously without yielding to the browser, potentially causing a long task (janky UI) while restoring a large session. 129. In restoreSid: if (m.role === 'tool' && m.is_tool_result) { ... if (content && content.includes('Search results for:')) { ... const urlMatches = [...content.matchAll(/URL: (https?:\/\/\S+)/g)]; — URL extraction uses \S+ which matches any nonwhitespace including punctuation at the end (e.g., http://example.com. with trailing period). The trailing period would be included in the URL incorrectly. 130. In restoreSid: if (m.has_image && !imgSrcs.length) { const badge = document.createElement('div'); badge.className = 'img-badge'; ... } — the class img-badge is used here but is not defined anywhere in the <style> block. The badge will render without any styling. 131. async function init() — calls localStorage.getItem(HK) and localStorage.getItem(DK) at startup. In private/incognito browsing on some iOS Safari versions, localStorage access throws a SecurityError. Although wrapped in try/catch, the catch block is catch (_) {} — silently ignores the error, leaving hmeta as an empty array (which is the fallback default and acceptable, but undocumented). 132. In init(): const knownSids = new Set(hmeta.map(h => h.sid)); followed by cleanup of deletedGroups entries for unknown sessions — this cleanup only runs on init(). If a session is deleted from the server (via the delete API) but the client still has a deletedGroups entry for it, it is not cleaned until init() runs again (page reload or first load). Minor stale data issue. 133. In init(): hmeta.sort((a, b) => (b.ts || 0) - (a.ts || 0)); — sessions fetched from the server are merged with local hmeta. The ts (timestamp) field from the server's response is used as s.updated_at. If the server returns updated_at as a date string (ISO 8601) rather than a Unix timestamp integer, (b.ts || 0) - (a.ts || 0) performs string subtraction (NaN), breaking the sort. No type validation is performed on s.updated_at. 134. In init(): closeSB() is called at the end, which is correct since the sidebar should start closed. But closeSB() calls closeSearch() which calls $('sb-q').value = '' and $('sb-q').blur() — calling .blur() on an element during page initialization when focus may not be on that element is harmless but unnecessary. 135. The second <script> block (context menu) is outside the IIFE of the first script block.
